speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: All electricity retailers must comply with the Code of Conduct for Retail Electricity Licensees, called the Code.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: EMA will not hesitate to investigate and take action against any non-compliance with the Code.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: For consumers who want greater certainty, we are also working with generation companies and electricity retailers to offer longer-term, fixed price contracts to consumers who wish to have more price stability.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: For example, retailers such as Keppel Electric and Sembcorp Power are currently offering longer-term electricity contracts ranging from six-months to three years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
text: Eligible consumers without a retail plan may wish to consider such contracts for greater price certainty.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Two, are gencos entitled to draw on EMA standby fuel facilities if they are not participating in TRECS?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There is no limit to the amount that can be drawn down for TRECS.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If their own gas supplies are disrupted, gencos can also draw on the Standby LNG Facility (SLF) and they have been doing so.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: They told me that it was fully subscribed that very day.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Can I confirm with the Minister, was TRECS fully subscribed for the month of Februrary and if so, how many businesses had to be turned away?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Are there plans to increase capacity for TRECS in the months of April and May, given the over-subscription in the month of March?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Lastly, taking into account the current global situation and over-subscribed TRECS, what measures has EMA planned to enhance Singapore's energy security and stabilise Singapore's wholesale electricity market?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: First, if he could get the resident or perhaps Mr Giam himself can write to me, I would be happy to investigate further.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For his resident who could not get access to the contract, as far as TRECS is concerned, I think there is a bit of a mismatch.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Moving forward, we have monitored it on a very tight basis.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Not only do we ensure that we have sufficient capacity as far as TRECS is concerned for the months of March, April and May, EMA has also been negotiating with other gencos to provide for fixed price contracts, on a longer-term basis, between three month and three years, as I shared in my earlier reply to Mr Yip Hon Weng.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: One of them is Keppel Electric and the other one is SembCorp Power.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Moving forward, in terms of ensuring our energy supplies and energy security, the fact is that there are further plans that are afoot.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: At this point in time, I am not ready to share these plans as yet.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In terms of looking at our standby facilities, in terms of negotiations with imports and so on, our entire team is on it.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To the extent to which we can share, so long as it does not compromise our ability to negotiate these contractual terms, at this point in time, it suffices for me to say that the entire energy team is working on a whole slew of measures to ensure that we do not get any disruptions in our energy supplies.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: Would the Ministry consider making participation in TRECS mandatory for all gencos?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As the name represents, it is a temporary situation; it is a temporary retail electricity contract scheme.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have made it voluntary because the nature of the generation of electrons is that if you require them to generate the electrons, if there is excess electrons, it gets wasted.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: You have on the one hand, companies who want to have some form of stability.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But there are also concerns about the high prices.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: What we need is a further, longer-term measure, which EMA has worked on pari passu, in terms of supporting.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Hence, we are quite comforted by the fact that two other gencos, gen retailers have stepped forth to offer longer-term fixed price contracts, ranging from six months to three years, to offer some form of price certainty.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The challenge is that today, TRECS offer the flexibility of a one-month contract, which allows companies to hedge for that one month.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Because the prices are quite high today, if they lock themselves for a long term, and if the price should ease off after that, then, it would be very difficult for them to justify that increased cost, moving forward.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Given the volatility that the current situation, the whole world is in today, with a lot of fluctuations happening, I think this is a more nuanced approach.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It allows responsiveness and the ability to nimbly work in terms of managing their costs, at least on a month-to-month basis, should the stability return to the market.
